code.originalText: Fourteen-week review: phlebotomy, the decision to stop drinking, mood and blood pressure

text.paragraph: Fourteen-week review: phlebotomy, stopping alcohol, mood and blood pressure. [S]

Mr. Hemingway returns fourteen weeks after intake and four weeks after the sick visit; the hand healed completely after the antibiotics. He came down by one drink a week as planned and has had no alcohol for three weeks. He had two nights of poor sleep after the last drink and no tremor, sweating or confusion. He keeps taking naltrexone and says the evening craving is weaker. He has had ten phlebotomies, with one skipped in the week of the hand infection, and the eleventh is planned after today's blood tests. Sertraline 100 mg causes no side effects; his mood is better and his PHQ-9 is 8, but no PHQ-9 had been done since the six-week visit. Home blood pressure averages 134/84. Headaches are down to one or two a week. His guns remain at the club. The echocardiogram has still not been done: the order went to an imaging center that never contacted him. [S]

S — Synthetic modern coding of DSM-5-TR severe alcohol use disorder (seven criteria); person-first language; not a claim about his real diagnosis.

Post-concussion symptoms (headaches, slowed thinking and forgetfulness) after repeated head injuries, most recently a concussion with a skull fracture a year ago; chronic traumatic encephalopathy is not diagnosed
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis anchored to his documented head injuries; alcohol and depression also affect the symptoms.

PHQ-9 monthly by the behavioral health clinician, recorded in the chart.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Diagnosis and management of hemochromatosis: 2011 practice guideline by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (2011); ACG Clinical Guideline: Hereditary Hemochromatosis (2019); The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Pharmacological Treatment of Patients With Alcohol Use Disorder (2018); The ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management (2020); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Major Depressive Disorder (2022); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management and Rehabilitation of Post-Acute Mild Traumatic Brain Injury (2021); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Weekly phlebotomy. Monthly PHQ-9 with the behavioral health clinician. Echocardiogram before the six-month visit. Preventive visit in seven weeks. Six-month review in twelve weeks with blood count, iron studies, liver tests, HbA1c, lipids, PHQ-9, AUDIT-C and MoCA. Next scheduled visit 1955-07-27: periodic adult preventive visit. [S]
